candidate_driver: Loss of customer transactions specific to stores S03, S04, S05
evidence_display: Observed and quantified; underlying cause UNRESOLVED
observed_effect: Transactions -25.5% vs matched controls (DiD); step change on 15 Jul 2025
what_we_know: Excess robust across 13 control-group and window variants; pre-trend slope p 0.93; placebo p 0.0015 (680 placebo groups); abrupt step (0-day transition) in all three stores within 12 days
what_we_do_not_know: The cluster was selected in Phase 5 because it declined most, so the placebo p-value (the smallest attainable) overstates significance; no matched control store is in Dublin (the cluster's region), and the Dublin control group has a different format. The cause is not observable
confidence: Range -EUR 435,210 to -EUR 377,245 across controls and windows
method: Difference-in-differences on store-week YoY log ratios; ratio DiD for EUR; daily change-point model
double_counting_risk: Would contain any above-control-rate stock-outs, returns or H&K effects in the cluster; in these data the cluster had less of each than the control rate implies, so no overlap is removed
conclusion: Confirmed and quantified: a sudden, uniform loss of receipts in three stores. The largest single driver.

driver: External / local cause of the cluster loss
candidate_driver: External local cause of the cluster traffic loss (competitor, access, local event)
evidence_display: HYPOTHESIS; cannot be tested with internal data
what_we_know: Pattern fits an outside cause: the transaction gap vs controls ranges -30 to -23 pp by weekday, -36 to -22 pp by hour and -32 to -24 pp by category (all strongly negative). Internal levers moved almost like the controls (cluster minus control change): availability +0.04 pp, promo revenue share +1.30 pp, ASP -0.86%, ranged SKUs -0.20%, return rate -0.63 pp
what_we_do_not_know: No direct evidence; an internal operational change not recorded in the model (e.g. opening hours, store works) would produce the same pattern
additional_data_required: Footfall counters, competitor openings and promotions near the three stores, road / access works, local events, store operating logs (hours, closures, refits)
conclusion: UNRESOLVED. Transaction loss remains unexplained after controlling for observable factors.

evidence_display: ROOT-CAUSE EVIDENCE for the stock-out mechanism; effect small
observed_effect: Full-week stock-out store-SKU-weeks 0 to 786; category availability 95.4% to 89.3%
what_we_know: Mechanism visible (no stock, no sales); estimator back-test 0.993; the gross estimate holds across the baseline variants with full coverage
what_we_do_not_know: After restock, Voltix Distribution Ltd SKUs sold above the expected rate (week 1 after: 1.06x expected, week 2 after: 1.38x expected). Allowing for the prior-year post-restock pattern, sales after episodes with a full-week stock-out ran EUR 13,272 above it: demand deferred rather than lost, which offsets 36% of the gross estimate. Substitution to other SKUs is not measured
confidence: Primary -EUR 44,460 to -EUR 23,963; upper bound -EUR 122,753 to -EUR 62,576 (not evidence)
method: Phase 5 in-stock baseline (seasonally adjusted, +/-4 to 13 weeks); full-week stock-outs only
additional_data_required: Daily stock positions to measure partial-week stock-outs; basket data on substitution
double_counting_risk: Would overlap the cluster excess only by the cluster's above-control-rate share (none here); no overlap with returns (different ledger line) or H&K (different category)
conclusion: Supported and robust: a real mechanism, but small: about 5% of the decline gross, and less net of the demand that returned after restock.

evidence_display: STATISTICAL ASSOCIATION; supplier responsibility NOT proven
observed_effect: SKU stock-out rate change +8.5 pp vs +1.6 pp for other suppliers' SKUs; mean opening stock of its SKUs fell while receipts per week did not
what_we_know: Difference +6.8 pp, 95% CI +2.5 to +11.2, permutation p 0.002 (0.010 after a Bonferroni adjustment for the 4 suppliers, since the supplier was picked as the worst before testing); survives leaving out any single SKU (min +6.1 pp)
what_we_do_not_know: Other deteriorating groups: Unknown supplier (2 SKUs) -21.8 pp. The data cannot say whether the supplier failed to deliver or Brightwater ordered less
method: SKU-level comparison vs other suppliers (bootstrap CI, permutation test, leave-one-SKU-out)
additional_data_required: Purchase orders, supplier confirmations and ASNs, delivery lead times and fill rates, Brightwater's own ordering parameters (min / max, safety stock) for these SKUs
conclusion: The concentration survives comparison with the other suppliers; whether supply or ordering caused it is a Hypothesis.

evidence_display: Observed increase; product defect remains a HYPOTHESIS
observed_effect: 'Faulty' refunds EUR 31,589 higher; recorded faulty rate per 100 units sold up in 5 stores (conditional binomial test, p < 0.01)
what_we_know: Top 5 stores hold 89% of the gross increase; 4 of 4 suppliers rose in the significant stores; there the 'Faulty' rate moved +2.84 and all other reasons +0.05 returned units per 100 sold; sale-to-return lag unchanged (KS p 0.60)
what_we_do_not_know: Spread over many products (top 5 hold only 53%); the till reason is not a verified defect
confidence: -EUR 31,589 to -EUR 26,226 depending on the rate basis
method: Rates per 100 units sold by product, supplier, store, sale cohort; conditional binomial tests of the rate increase (both years' rates uncertain)
additional_data_required: QA inspection results, batch / lot or serial numbers, supplier defect and RMA reports, warranty claims, store returns-handling audits
double_counting_risk: Returns ledger, separate from lost sales; the cluster's own 'Faulty' refunds changed -EUR 4,937 (below the control-store rate), so no overlap with the cluster excess is removed
conclusion: Concentrated in a few stores and recent sale cohorts, across products: consistent with either a local product batch or a change in how those stores record returns. Cause is a Hypothesis.

candidate_driver: Product quality problem vs store recording practice behind 'Faulty' returns
evidence_display: HYPOTHESIS; needs QA, batch and RMA data
what_we_know: In the stores with significant increases, 4 of 4 suppliers rose, while the largest holds 68% of the increase: neither a single-supplier defect nor a store- or distribution-side cause can be excluded
additional_data_required: QA inspection results, batch / lot or serial numbers, supplier defect and RMA reports, warranty claims, store returns-handling audits, and the distribution centre / delivery route serving these stores

candidate_driver: Home & Kitchen promotion programme (deeper, more frequent discounts)
evidence_display: STATISTICAL ASSOCIATION only; methods disagree in sign
observed_effect: Discount rate on gross sales 2.4% to 11.9%; H&K sales -7.1% vs control categories in the same store-weeks, units -1.7%
what_we_know: M1 DiD 95% CI -EUR 248,937 to -EUR 121,581; pre-period gap slope +0.0008 log points a week; units -1.7% (CI -4.1% to +0.8%), so the fall is mostly price; M4 discount accounting -EUR 265,003
what_we_do_not_know: Event-level (M3 EUR 79,059) and dose-response (M2 EUR 97,505) methods say the extra promotions ADDED revenue. Their baselines are exposed to back-to-back promotions (64% of current-year events follow another promotion of the same store-SKU within the baseline window), but the disagreement is real
confidence: Range -EUR 380,272 to EUR 97,505; sign depends on method
method: M1 category DiD; M2 dose-response; M3 event-level; M4 discount-rate accounting
additional_data_required: Promotion calendar with objectives, planned vs actual depth, a controlled test (holdout stores) or at least SKU-level price elasticities
double_counting_risk: Different category from D03 / D05; the cluster's share is below the control-store rate, so no overlap with the cluster excess is removed
conclusion: Associated with the H&K decline and plausible, but not established: the counterfactual is method-dependent.

candidate_driver: Range and distribution change in Electronics & Tech
evidence_display: Observed change; SKU switching is a HYPOTHESIS
observed_effect: Outside the cluster, category sales -EUR 124,543: delisted SKUs -EUR 95,472, new SKUs EUR 265,233, continuing SKUs -EUR 294,304 (fewer ranged store-SKU-weeks -EUR 28,774; lower sales per ranged store-SKU-week -EUR 265,530)
what_we_know: Measured SKU by SKU (FACT). New Voltix Distribution Ltd SKUs EUR 252,306 while its continuing SKUs -EUR 210,136: consistent with customers switching to the new models
what_we_do_not_know: Competing explanations for the continuing-SKU fall: partial-week stock-outs (not in the primary lost-sales estimate), substitution to new SKUs while older ones were out of stock, and switching between models; none can be separated without daily stock and customer-level data
method: SKU status by presence in each H2; distribution effect = change in ranged store-SKU-weeks x prior-year sales per ranged week
additional_data_required: Range plan and delisting dates, customer-level purchase history (switching between models)
double_counting_risk: A partition of the category change; not added to the attribution. The unexplained part sits in the residual (D09)
conclusion: The range churn itself added revenue outside the cluster (new SKUs more than replaced delisted ones); the decline sits in continuing SKUs. Whether new SKUs took their sales, partial-week stock-outs or substitution during stock-outs explain it is a Hypothesis.

candidate_driver: Residual: change not attributed to the drivers above
evidence_display: Not attributed; mostly Electronics outside the cluster
observed_effect: Other stores: Electronics & Tech change not explained by stock-outs or 'Faulty' returns -EUR 88,168; Other stores: Home & Kitchen change not explained by the category-specific (M1) change EUR 40,069; Other stores: other categories (no driver identified) EUR 461; Store cluster: change at the control-store rate, net of the cluster's driver amounts -EUR 30,884
what_we_know: Closes the exclusive attribution exactly; outside the cluster, categories other than E&T and H&K were flat, so this is not estate-wide softness
confidence: Absorbs the uncertainty of every component
method: Total minus exclusive components; split by where it sits
additional_data_required: Daily stock positions per SKU, customer-level purchase history (switching between E&T models), market data for E&T
conclusion: Not attributed. Mostly E&T continuing-SKU sales outside the cluster (see D08).
